questions.text: Your team has two weeks for a project and nobody has started yet. What do you do?

answers.text: I study the problem first and work out the smartest approach before anyone starts.
I just start with whatever sparks my interest and let the momentum carry the others along.
I take on the part that matters most for the result and drive it forward myself.
I stay calm, see what each person naturally brings and let the work find its own rhythm.
I get everyone together, split the tasks fairly and make sure each person knows their part.

questions.text: You are choosing between several job offers. What tips the balance for you?

answers.text: A team where I feel at home and a job that fits the natural rhythm of my life.
A workplace with fair rules, where people keep their word and look out for each other.
The chance to keep learning and to become really good at something demanding.
Work that excites me and leaves me free to do things in my own way.
The pay, the career prospects and how much say I will have in the decisions.

questions.text: Which of these bothers you the most?

answers.text: When people make decisions without thinking them through first.
When people hide what they really feel behind polite phrases.
When people wait for others to sort out their problems for them.
When people change things that work just for the sake of change.
When people break their promises or treat others unfairly.

questions.text: Your neighbour's tree hangs far over your garden and blocks the sun. What do you do?

answers.text: I tell them clearly what I need and what I am willing to offer in return.
I plant something that loves the shade; the tree was there long before me.
I check what the local rules say and politely ask them to keep to them.
I work out a solution that would suit both gardens and bring along a sketch.
I go straight over and tell them honestly that it really bothers me.

questions.text: You are planning a big celebration for your birthday. What matters most to you?

answers.text: That it is thoughtfully planned and well organised, down to the last detail.
That it is wild and spontaneous, and nobody wants to go home at the end.
That everything is exactly the way I want it; it is my day, after all.
That it feels warm and familiar, with the people and traditions I love.
That everyone who matters is invited and nobody ends up feeling left out.

questions.text: You start at a new workplace. What do you notice most in the first week?

answers.text: Whether the rules are clear and everyone is treated the same way.
Where things are done inefficiently and could clearly be improved.
Whether people actually enjoy what they do and have some passion.
Who really makes the decisions and where the opportunities lie.
How people treat each other, and whether it feels like I could belong.

questions.text: You have managed to save up a good sum of money. What do you do with it?

answers.text: I use it to put down roots: a home, a garden, something that will last for years.
I keep a safety cushion for my family and give some of it to a cause I believe in.
I research the options thoroughly and invest where the numbers make the most sense.
I spend part of it on an experience I have been dreaming about for a long time.
I put it into something that increases my independence and my future options.

questions.text: You are thinking about volunteering in your free time. What would be your reason?

answers.text: I feel responsible for my community and want to do my fair share for it.
I want to understand a problem properly and help to solve it really well.
Something moves me deeply, and I simply cannot stand by and do nothing.
It builds skills and contacts that will help me get further in life.
I want to protect something I care about, like a local park or an old custom.

questions.text: You follow the news about a big political decision. What do you pay attention to first?

answers.text: How it will affect people's lives and what I feel when I hear about it.
What it means for me personally and how I can best make use of it.
Whether it respects what has grown over generations or throws it away.
Whether it is fair and whether it was decided in the proper way.
Whether the facts behind it hold up and where it will lead in the long run.

questions.text: You want to learn to cook a dish you loved on holiday. How do you go about it?

answers.text: I find a proper recipe and follow it step by step, exactly as it is written.
I read up on why the ingredients work together and experiment until it is perfect.
I throw in whatever feels right and taste as I go; the fun is in the cooking.
I ask the best cook I know to show me their tricks, so I get good at it quickly.
I ask someone from that region how their family has always made it and stick to that.

questions.text: You look back on a really good year. What made it such a good one?

answers.text: I lived intensely, followed my heart and did things I will never forget.
I reached the goals I had set myself and am clearly better off than before.
I felt at peace with myself and content with the way my life is going.
I kept my commitments and was there for the people who relied on me.
I came to understand many things better and grew noticeably wiser.

questions.text: Think of someone you really admire. What stands out most about them?

answers.text: Their drive: they built their life with their own two hands.
Their calm: they are content and have nothing to prove to anyone.
Their integrity: they stand up for others and for what is right.
Their mind: they understand things others do not even notice.
Their boldness: they live fully and are not afraid to show it.

questions.text: At a family gathering, two relatives start a heated argument. What do you do?

answers.text: I say openly what I think about it, even if that heats things up for a moment.
I make it clear I will not take sides and keep my own evening from being spoiled.
I suggest a walk outside for everyone; storms like this usually blow over by themselves.
I step in and make sure both of them get a fair chance to say their piece.
I listen closely, figure out what the real misunderstanding is and point it out.

questions.text: What would you most like the people who know you well to say about you?

answers.text: That I know exactly what I want and find a way to get it.
That I am grounded and patient, and at home in who I am.
That you can always count on me to stand up for what is right.
That I see things clearly and think further ahead than most people.
That I am full of life and always honest about how I feel.

questions.text: You come home after a long trip abroad. What strikes you first?

answers.text: How good it feels to be back among familiar people and places.
How orderly and reliable everything is here compared to the trip.
Which ideas I saw abroad would work better here as well.
How much I already miss the adventure and the unknown.
Which of my experiences will be useful to me from now on.
